prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a hit while turning left. Plain text. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1043; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant [INSURER], subject to its policy of insurance with Plaintiff, files this Original Answer to Plaintiff's Original Petition and respectfully shows the Court as follows.

General Denial. Pursuant to Texas Rule of Civil Procedure 92, Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict proof thereof by a preponderance of the evidence.

Affirmative Defenses. First, Plaintiff's alleged injuries were caused, in whole or in part, by the negligence of Plaintiff, who failed to keep a proper lookout, failed to yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic while turning left, and failed to maintain control of the vehicle. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced by Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility. Second, Defendant invokes proportionate responsibility, and any judgment against Defendant must be limited to its percentage of responsibility, if any. Third, Defendant asserts its right to a credit or offset for all sums paid or payable to Plaintiff by or on behalf of any settling person or responsible third party.

Defendant reserves the right to amend this Answer as discovery proceeds.
